note: Former state park returned to Mitchell County, 6 mi east of Osage and 4 mi north on Shadow Ave. Gravel sites; enclosed stone shelter house with electric; playground. The Little Cedar River is about 100-130 m south of the loop across a meadow, not at the sites. --Claude
summary: The county pages confirm $15/night, water and electric at every site (50/30/20A), pit toilets plus a shower house (conservation site), early May to mid October. They disagree on the site count (8 vs 7). The derived 'bookable online' is not supported: no Pioneer site is in the county's booking system, so reservable was cleared. Not waterfront stands; phone 641-732-5204.
flags: BOOKING: derived reservable:true (from the old note's 'bookable online') cleared. The county's 'Book Campsite' link goes to mycountyparks' Mitchell facility search, which lists Cedar Bridge Park campsites 1-19, Riverside and Pinicon Alders but no Pioneer Park site, and the Pioneer Park mycountyparks page has no facility to book. No page states FCFS either, so nothing was written in its place. The conservation page's 'Book your stay now' is generic copy.

SITE COUNT CONFLICT: mitchellcountyconservation.com says '8 spacious gravel sites'; mycountyparks says '7 designated gravel campsites'. Both are official, so the stored count (7, derived) was left alone.

WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' confirmed against the conservation page's 'Nestled right on the banks of the picturesque Little Cedar River' (marketing; it triggered the re-audit). On NAIP the camp loop (~43.3411,-92.6800, RVs visible) sits in a clearing with a tree line and a 100-130 m meadow between it and the Little Cedar, which is about 15-20 m wide (creek-sized) there.
